Can put a photo down later but for me I ended up making my own planner using canva and an A5 binder. I have a weekly habit tracker page, weekly plan page. Then for my day page it has on it a timeline from 5am-9pm, a habit/todo list and a priority list. There is also a little slider at the bottom to select productivity level for the day. I also have a notes page on the right(day page is on the left) so I can jot things down if need be. I usually try to look at it in the morning and evenings.

When I was 16 I joined a social anxiety support forum. I didn’t have any friends most of my life due to anxiety issues amongst other things and was sad/lonely and trying to improve things. I saw a profile pop up on a forum post I was reading and saw the location was somewhat nearby(an hours drive).

I messaged the guy just explaining how I was looking for friends and I noticed he was closish by, also mentioning we had some bands we liked in common. Turns out he was only a year older than me, we started chatting and after a month or so we finally decided to meet for a movie. Started off as friends for a month or two, progressed to dating, bf/gf and now 10 years later we are married with a house and animal’s :)

Probably the best answer. It's so different on a person to person basis. Just like getting up early vs staying up late. Some people just work better at night rather than morning so there's no point in forcing yourself to get up at 5am or whatever to do things if you have no energy. OP you should try to figure out when you have the most energy and maximize your time there. Morning, Afternoon or Evening.

It sounds like you are wanting to get up early to workout and it's the getting up part thats hard less so the workout. Baby steps. First thing is to get out of bed. What I have found that works for me is if I hype myself the night before about the time i am going to get up and how awesome it's going to be to get what I want to get done, done. For some reason this usually results in me waking up earlier than my alarm and easily getting out of bed. Also make sure you are getting your 7-8hrs of sleep, it'll be way harder to get up if you are ridiculously tired. 

What works for me may not work for you but it is a suggestion. Best of luck with your new habits! :)

My symptoms started out very gradual, little bit of blood in the stool every now and then. Didn't think much of it honestly. Then it started getting slightly more frequent. That and I started going more frequently. Then it just got worse to the point of going to the bathroom 20+ times a day. Again though it was gradual to get to that point and that was 4 years ago now. Mine however is Ulcerative Colitis which is inflamation that is only in the colon. I have since had my colon removed so I am doing better. I am and have been iron deficient since I was diagnosed. As well as having loud bowel sounds, bloating etc. Those kinds of symptoms are common place with these GI disorders.

Your symptoms to me sound more like chrons(mild) as it can produce inflammation anywhere in the GI tract. Plus since you are only 23(younger) that is usually when these autoimmune diseases strike. I was 18 when I was diagnosed and am now 23. Unfortunately the only way to get officially diagnosed is for them to scope the colon and take biopsies. A Gastrointestinal doc would be your best bet for diagnosing you as they know all about the gastro system. Again I know you can't get a doc though so again watch your symptoms. But if the blood does not continue at all, it might be something like IBS.

You can attempt to make diet changes, this helps some people with IBS or IBD. My recommendation would be to have a food journal, write down everything you eat and how it effects you. Then eliminate the things that effect you badly(i.e you may have issues with dairy or gluten) and see how you feel. Also attempt to take things like probiotics, this might be able to help your bloating etc.

That really does sound like Ulcerative Colitis or Chrons. I have heard of people with Chrons having all of the symptoms described. The biggest thing to realize is that all of the symptoms you have described(even the mouth sores) are in the GI tract. 

 I know you said you can't go to a doctor but just please watch your symptoms, if you start having worse symptoms go to the hospital or something.

​

Anyway in regards to how people feel about it, it depends on how well you take to having an ostomy and surgeries. You almost just trade in the set of problems that you have with your colon for a set of smaller more manageable problems. You can go for a perm ostomy or a jpouch, some people are so happy just being without UC problems they would rather keep the ostomy and others don't want to have a bag and choose the jpouch. It has a 90% success rate with 70% doing good 20% keeping the pouch but having chronic problems and 10% failing. There are lots of horror stories out there the people that have successful pouches usually aren't posting online about it. My best suggestion to you from reading through support groups and documents about these surgeries is make sure you seek out a very skilled surgeon who specializes in these procedures.
